terms.comment: Our phrase, with the ancient adjective pōmārius: mēnsa is the classical word for the table goods are sold from (Lewis & Short: “a market-stand for meat, vegetables, etc.”; mēnsa laniōnia, a butcher’s stall, Suet. Claud. 15). Morgan–Owens has taberna pōmāria (below); a taberna is a booth or shop built of boards.

sources: Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. produce stand, fruit stand.
Lewis & Short: mensa · Lewis & Short: pomarius · Lewis & Short: taberna
